Answer: Entailment
Confidence: 90%

The statute in Section 3306(a)(1)(B) defines an employer as someone who employed at least one individual on each of some 10 days during the calendar year, with each day being in a different calendar week. Alice employed Bob on 12 occasions in 2017, spanning 11 different calendar weeks (Jan 24=W4, Feb 4=W5, Mar 3=W9, Mar 18=W11, Apr 1=W13, May 9=W19, Oct 14=W41, Oct 25=W43, Nov 8=W45, Nov 22=W47, Dec 1=W48), meeting the 10-day threshold with each day in a different calendar week. The answer is Entailment since the claim that Section 3306(a)(1)(B) applies to Alice for 2017 is true based on the statute and facts. The main risk would be if the week-counting method differs from ISO weeks (e.g., using Sunday-start weeks), but even then all 12 dates are 1-2 weeks apart so they would still span at least 10 different weeks.
